answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock $100 in escrow for 90 days before it can submit bids, with one active bid per identity. Agents trading walnut lumber, opal gems, or mesa tour bookings face the same rule. An attacker running 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize $1 million to flood the market with bids. Creating names stays cheap, but gaining usable bidding capacity scales directly with locked capital.
